title: Installing Prisma in Next.js
description: Step-by-step setup of Prisma in a modern Next.js 14/15 App Router project with TypeScript and PostgreSQL.

data.text: Setting up Prisma inside a Next.js application requires installing two distinct packages: the **Prisma CLI** (as a development dependency) to handle migrations, introspection, and code generation, and the **Prisma Client** (as a production runtime dependency) to execute database queries.

data.caption: Prisma Setup Flow in Next.js
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[npm install prisma] --> B[npx prisma init]
    B --> C[Configure .env DATABASE_URL]
    C --> D[Define Models in schema.prisma]
    D --> E[npx prisma migrate dev]
    E --> F[Generate PrismaClient Singleton]

data.title: Terminal Commands
data.content: Install prisma as a devDependency and @prisma/client as a standard dependency.
data.code:
# Using npm
npm install -D prisma
npm install @prisma/client

# Or using Yarn
yarn add -D prisma
yarn add @prisma/client

# Or using pnpm
pnpm add -D prisma
pnpm add @prisma/client

data.text: Run the init command to bootstrap the configuration files. By default, you can specify your database provider (e.g. `postgresql`, `mysql`, `sqlite`).

data.title: Initialize with PostgreSQL
data.content: This creates the prisma/schema.prisma file and adds a DATABASE_URL variable to your .env file.

data.text: Open the `.env` file generated at the project root and provide your PostgreSQL connection URI. If using a cloud database like Neon, Supabase, or AWS RDS, paste your connection string here:

data.title: .env Connection String Structure
data.content: Ensure special characters in passwords (like @ or :) are URL encoded.

data.title: Git Security Checklist
data.text: Never commit your `.env` file containing database passwords to version control! Ensure `.env` is listed in your `.gitignore`.

items.hint: Test database connectivity with `npx prisma db pull` or `migrate`

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `npx prisma init` sets up the schema and `.env` template.
Always match your schema datasource provider with your actual database engine.
